what_its_for: Dicyclomine is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). It helps relax the muscles in your stomach and intestines to reduce painful cramping, bloating, and stomach spasms.
how_to_take: Take dicyclomine by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully with a special measuring spoon or oral syringe — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 20 mg taken 4 times a day (before or with meals and at bedtime). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to 40 mg four times a day if needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store dicyclomine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the liquid form.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking dicyclomine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, because dicyclomine can reduce sweating and raise your body temperature. Avoid antacids within 1 hour of taking dicyclomine, as they may reduce how well it works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty urinating or inability to urinate, severe constipation, confusion or hallucinations, eye pain or vision changes, severe dizziness or fainting, high fever or hot dry skin (signs of overheating), skin rash or allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also contact your doctor if your IBS symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks.
when_it_works: Dicyclomine usually starts working within 1 to 2 hours after taking a dose. You may begin to notice relief from stomach cramps and spasms fairly quickly, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults are more sensitive to side effects like confusion, dizziness, constipation, and difficulty urinating. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do NOT use dicyclomine if you are breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing infant. Children: Dicyclomine is NOT recommended for infants under 6 months of age and should be used with great caution in young children. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed.
